p.i: non pauca sunt flumina, quæ cum longo interuallo apparent, tandem alicubi se abscondant in terræ uisceribus, & non multo post iterum emerguntiut [?] Lycus amnis in Asia, Erasinus in Argolica, Tygris in Mesopotamia.

main_text.head: Quas ob causas tum aquæ, tum terræ, interdum longo temporis progressu locum mutant?

p.i: Compertum est, quibus locis nunc mare est uel aliæ aquæ, ijsdem fuisse olim uastam terram: & uice uersa, ubi nunc terra est, ibi quondam fuisse aquas. Sic antiquitus tota Ægyptus urbe, quam Thebas uocant, constabat, teste etiam Lib.I. cap.14 Homero: nunc uero latissimè patet, multis undiq; terris circumpositis, &c. Itaq; huius mutationis causæ dignæ sunt inquisitione.

main_text.p: 1. Causa formalis: Quemadmodum plantæ & animalia à cœlo præcipuè accipiunt suæ conditionis & alterationis modum, ut primùm quidè quasi in iuuenta floreát, deinde robur ac magnitudinè tanquàm uirilem ætatem induant, tandem uero quasi senio languescát atq; extinguantur: ita terra & aqua calore atq; frigore à Solis siderumq; motu proueniên tibus uariè afficiuntur, ac terra quidem modò quasi in uirenti ætate humore undique perfunditur, modò uero quasi senio confecta arescit & siccatur: aquæ autem aliquando uno loco cedūt, moxq; alium locum nouum occupant.

page.notes: The printed page number is small and partly unclear; read as 323 (possibly 325). The marginal note reads "Lib.I." with "cap.14" beneath it. The word "emerguntiut" is printed as shown and is doubtful. The signature "x 2" at the foot is partly faint. The question paragraph is set in larger roman type, so it is treated as a level 2 heading. The paragraph "1. Causa formalis" is a numbered paragraph, not a heading.
